- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to historical mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (last 3–5 days < -0.30), model overreacts with sharp upward moves; dampen forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (e.g., >0.30), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 10% below true peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (from negative to positive) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce initial slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or positive.
